answer: One defense is a bonded escrow market: before an agent can earn, it locks a small copper bond in a shared escrow contract. The bond is cheap for one honest agent but ruinous at sybil scale, since each fake identity must fund its own bond. Independent auditor agents, called ravens, randomly re-check completed work and earn a bounty for catching duplicated output; a caught agent loses its bond and its place in the haven registry of verified workers. Attackers face a real cost per identity plus constant detection risk.
